prompt: Make me an app like bit.ly. Sketch a small planned SaaS architecture using the planning library: owners create and manage short links, visitors follow them and owners see click activity. Include C1 actors, described C2 containers with proposed technology and verb/protocol relationships, and cohesive C3 responsibilities in the API. This is a planning study; no runtime implementation or generation is requested. Choose reasonable defaults and complete the sketch in this turn.
reply:
I’ll sketch a small web app, API and database, with API responsibilities for owner access, link management, redirects and click activity. All technology choices will be proposals for this planning study.

Completed the sketch: C1 owner and visitor actors, three described C2 containers with proposed technologies and labeled protocol relationships, and four cohesive API responsibilities covering access, link management, redirects and click activity.

Only expected planning-only generation findings remain. No runtime implementation was created.

activity.summary: Applied 7 changes as one undo step

elements.name: Owner web app
elements.notes: Provide sign-up/sign-in, a cursor-paginated links list, create/edit/disable actions, copy-short-URL action, and a per-link activity page with UTC date filters. Show validation errors, alias conflicts, empty activity, loading and retry states. Never expose another owner's records. Dashboard freshness follows successful click writes; activity is approximate, not unique visitors.
elements.description: Lets owners sign in, create and manage short links, and view click activity.

elements.name: Short links API
elements.notes: Planning only; no runtime is supplied. Use separate proposed public origins for dashboard/API and short URLs. Owner access: POST /v1/accounts, POST /v1/sessions, DELETE /v1/sessions/current; hash passwords with Argon2id, use opaque server-side sessions with Secure HttpOnly SameSite cookies, CSRF protection and explicit dashboard CORS allowlist. Rate-limit login, link creation and public resolution. Link management: POST/GET /v1/links, GET/PATCH /v1/links/:id; derive owner_id from the session and scope every management/activity query by it. Return 404 for inaccessible records. Support destination, optional custom alias and expiry, and disabling. Validate absolute http/https destinations, reject credentials and own short-domain loops; never fetch destinations. Generate random base62 codes with a unique constraint and bounded collision retries; custom alias conflicts return 409. Reserve system paths and do not reuse disabled codes. Public GET /:code returns 302 with Location and Cache-Control: no-store; unknown is 404 and disabled/expired is 410. HEAD resolves without counting. For successful GET resolution, invoke click recording with a short bounded database timeout before replying; recording failure must not prevent redirect, so totals may undercount. Do not claim exactly-once counting or unique visitors. Activity: GET /v1/links/:id/activity?from=&to=&bucket=day, owner-only, UTC, bounded to 90 days, totals and daily buckets with zeros for empty days. Aggregate on demand from retained events. A click means a successful redirect request; bots and repeat requests may count. Retain events for 90 days; design a daily bounded cleanup task inside the API with database-coordinated single-run locking. No queue, cache or separate worker is needed for the initial planning scope. Capacity and latency remain unspecified and unverified.
elements.description: Owns accounts, owner-scoped link management, public redirects and click activity queries.

elements.name: Links and activity database
elements.notes: Proposed schema: accounts(id,email unique,password_hash,created_at); sessions(token_hash unique,owner_id,expires_at); links(id,owner_id,code unique,destination,created_at,updated_at,expires_at,disabled_at); clicks(id,link_id,occurred_at,referrer_host nullable). Index links(owner_id,created_at,id) for cursor pages and clicks(link_id,occurred_at) for date-bounded aggregates. Enforce foreign keys, code uniqueness and transactional link updates. Public lookup exposes only resolution fields; management queries require owner scope. Do not retain raw IP addresses, full referrer URLs or user-agent strings. Store only a validated referrer hostname if present; label activity as request counts. Purge click events after 90 days and expired sessions daily. Backup retention proposal: 30 days; restore procedures and recovery objectives require later design and testing.
elements.description: Stores owner accounts, sessions, short-link mappings and recent click events.

annotations.text: Planning study only. Three proposed containers and four API responsibilities. PostgreSQL is the authoritative store; activity is computed on demand from 90 days of minimal events. Redirects continue when click recording fails, so counts are approximate. Single-region availability is a proposal; capacity, latency and recovery need later validation. Planned families provide no runtime and block generation. Billing, custom domains and advanced abuse review are deferred.
